'''Tata Communications Limited''' (formerly known as '''Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited''') is an Indian [[telecommunications]] company, headquartered in [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]]. It was a government-owned telecommunications service provider before being sold to the [[Tata Group]] in 2002 under the [[Third Vajpayee ministry]] government.<ref name="frontline">{{cite news |title=Privatisation and primitive accumulation |url=https://frontline.thehindu.com/columns/article30245162.ece |publisher=[[Frontline (magazine)|Frontline]] |date=June 8, 2002}}</ref>

The company provides network, cloud, cybersecurity, media, Internet of Things (IoT), collaboration and digital infrastructure services to enterprises and service providers worldwide.<ref name="livemint"/> It is listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] and the [[National Stock Exchange of India]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Tata Communications Ltd Stock Price and Key Metrics |url=https://www.screener.in/company/TATACOMM/consolidated/ |work=Screener.in}}</ref>

Tata Communications operates a [[Tier 1 network|Tier-1 IP network]] and a wholly owned subsea fibre-optic cable system spanning over 500,000 kilometres (310,000 miles).<ref>{{cite news |last=Abbas |first=Muntazir |title=Tata Communications seeks government support for urgent undersea cable repairs |url=https://telecom.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/telecom-equipment/tata-communications-seeks-government-support-for-urgent-undersea-cable-repairs/126053397 |work=[[The Economic Times|ET Telecom]] |date=18 December 2025}}</ref> It provides services to enterprises across more than 190 countries and territories.<ref name="fortuneindia"/>
==History==
[[File:Videsh Sanchar Nigam headquarters, Bombay (2006).jpg|250px|thumb|Headquarters of VSNL in Mumbai, 2006]]

The business was founded as Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited (VSNL) in March 1986 by the [[Government of India]] as a public-sector undertaking to manage the country's international telecommunications services.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Block |first=Daniel |date=1 February 2019 |title=How Reliance Jio is monopolising the telecom sector |url=https://caravanmagazine.in/reportage/government-helping-reliance-jio-monopolise-telecom |access-date=2019-05-21 |website=The Caravan |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sridhar |first=V. |title=Challenges of change |url=https://frontline.thehindu.com/the-nation/article30160711.ece |website=[[Frontline (magazine)|Frontline]] | date=9 January 1998}}</ref> It took over the operations of the Overseas Communications Service, a company under the Ministry of Communications.<ref>{{cite book |last=Hudson |first=Heather E. |title=Global Connections: International Telecommunications Infrastructure and Policy |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Global_Connections/Oq21AAAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=VSNL+Overseas+Communications+Service&dq=VSNL+Overseas+Communications+Service&printsec=frontcover |page=294 |publisher=[[Van Nostrand Reinhold]] |year=1997}}</ref> Under the chairmanship of [[B. K. Syngal]] (1991–98),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mookerji |first=Nivedita |date=16 May 2020 |title=What Telecom Man reveals about India's business-politics links |url=https://www.rediff.com/money/special/what-telecom-man-reveals-about-indias-business-politics-links/20200516.htm |access-date=2022-07-11 |website=[[Rediff]] |language=en}}</ref> VSNL launched the first publicly available internet service in [[India]] in August 1995.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 August 1995 |title=VSNL starts India's first Internet service today |url=http://www.dxm.org/techonomist/news/vsnlnow.html |access-date=2022-07-11 |website=www.dxm.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=10 July 2022 |title='Father of Indian Internet' BK Syngal passes away |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/former-vsnl-chief-bk-syngal-passes-away/article65623246.ece |access-date=2022-07-11 |website=[[The Hindu BusinessLine]] |language=en}}</ref>

After the [[Government of India]] launched its [[Disinvestment of Public Sector Units in India|disinvestment programme]], VSNL was acquired by the [[Tata Group]] in 2002.<ref name="frontline"/> The international arm of VSNL, known as VSNL International, was established in 2004. The company was subsequently renamed Tata Communications on 13 February 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Form 20-F |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1116134/000119312508209835/d20f.htm |access-date=2023-07-05 |website=www.sec.gov}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2007-10-31 |title=VSNL to be named Tata Communications |work=[[The Economic Times]] |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/vsnl-to-be-named-tata-communications/articleshow/2506375.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-07-05 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

In August 2009, Tata Communications and Tyco Telecommunications completed the 6,700 km TGN-Intra Asia (TGN-IA) submarine cable system, connecting [[Singapore]], [[Hong Kong]], [[Tokyo]], [[Vietnam]] and the [[Philippines]]. The system was designed to provide resilient and diverse network routes that bypass seismically active areas near [[Taiwan]].<ref>{{cite news |last=PK |first=Tarun |title=Tata Communications completes “TGN-Intra Asia” |url=https://telecomtalk.info/tata-communications-completes-6700km-tgn-intra-asia/7872/ |work=TelecomTalk |date=19 August 2009}}</ref>

In 2014, the company launched IZO, a cloud connectivity platform designed to enable enterprises to securely connect to multiple cloud service providers over a single network.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Comm launches private cloud services on IZO platform |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/internet/tata-comm-launches-private-cloud-services-on-izo-platform/articleshow/49572079.cms |work=[[The Economic Times]] |date=29 October 2015}}</ref> In February 2017, it sold its South African telecommunications subsidiary, [[Neotel]], to [[Liquid Telecom Group]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications completes sale of Neotel for Rs 3,200 crore |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/tata-communications-completes-sale-of-neotel-for-rs-3200-crore/articleshow/57088255.cms |work=[[The Economic Times]] |date=10 February 2017}}</ref>

In March 2021, the [[Government of India]] exited its remaining 26.12% stake in Tata Communications, ending its shareholding in the company nearly two decades after its privatisation in 2002.<ref>{{cite news |title=Government sells 10% stake to exit Tata Communications |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/government-sells-10-stake-to-exit-tata-communications/articleshow/81589443.cms |work=[[The Times of India]] |date=19 March 2021}}</ref>  In March 2025, it launched Vayu, a cloud fabric platform designed to support enterprise multi-cloud environments and artificial intelligence workloads.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications unveils Vayu, an overall AI Cloud offering for enterprises |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/tata-communications-unveils-vayu-an-overall-ai-cloud-offering-for-enterprises/article69353399.ece |work=The Hindu |date=21 March 2025}}</ref>

=== Acquisitions ===
In 2004, then operating as VSNL, the company acquired the broadband assets of [[DishnetDSL]] for ₹270 crore in a slump sale from its promoter Chinnakannan Sivasankaran.<ref>{{Cite news|title=VSNL acquires assets of DishnetDSL for Rs 270 cr |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/focus/it-cities/mumbai/vsnl-acquires-assets-of-dishnetdsl-for-rs-270-cr/articleshow/571495.cms |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=19 March 2004}}</ref>

In 2005, the company acquired the Tyco Global Network, an undersea fibre-optic cable system spanning approximately 60,000 kilometres, for approximately US$130 million.<ref name="Rediff">{{cite news |title=VSNL completes Tyco acquisition |url=https://m.rediff.com/business/report/vsnl/20050701.htm |publisher=[[Rediff.com]]|date=July 1, 2005}}</ref> The acquisition formed the backbone of what became the Tata Global Network and significantly extended the company's international reach.<ref name="Rediff" /> In 2006, it acquired Teleglobe International Holdings, a provider of international voice, data and value-added services, for approximately US$178 million.<ref>{{cite web |title=Form 20-F: Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1116134/000119312506201053/d20f.htm |publisher=[[United States Securities and Exchange Commission]] |date=September 29, 2006}}</ref>

In July 2008, the company entered into an agreement with [[Eskom]] and [[Transnet]] to acquire their combined 30% stake in South African telecommunications operator [[Neotel]]. In January 2009, the company completed the acquisition, increasing its shareholding and becoming Neotel's controlling shareholder.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Comm buys controlling stake in SA company |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/news-archive/web/tata-comm-buys-controlling-stake-in-sa-company/ |work=[[The Indian Express]] |date=20 January 2009}}</ref>

In 2011, Tata Communications acquired BitGravity, a United States-based [[content delivery network]] provider. The company had previously invested US$11.5 million in BitGravity in 2008 as part of a strategic partnership.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications completes acquisition of BitGravity |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/K6ulXvifXcsuHiTCgmmnyK/Tata-Communications-completes-acquisition-of-BitGravity.html |work=[[Mint (newspaper)|Mint]] |date=February 16, 2011}}</ref> The company acquired Teleena, a [[Netherlands]]-based [[Internet of things|IoT]] and [[Mobile virtual network operator|Mobile Virtual Network Enabler]] (MVNE) company in 2018.<ref name="toi">{{cite news |title=Tata Comm fully acquires Netherlands-based IoT firm Teleena |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/tata-comm-fully-acquires-netherlands-based-iot-firm-teleena/articleshow/66058332.cms |work=The Times of India |agency=PTI |date=October 3, 2018}}</ref> The company had previously invested in Teleena in January 2017, acquiring a 35 per cent stake. The acquisition enabled Tata Communications to access Teleena's mobile virtual network enabler platform and related technology.<ref name="toi"/>

In 2020, Tata Communications bought an initial majority stake of 58.1% in Oasis Smart SIM, an [[eSIM]] technology company.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications buys 58.1% stake in French e-SIM tech company |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/telecom-news/tata-communications-buys-58-1-stake-in-french-e-sim-tech-company/articleshow/79926035.cms |work=[[The Economic Times]] |date=23 December 2020}}</ref> The acquisition was completed in 2023 when the company acquired the remaining 41.9% shares.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications to take full control of Oasis Smart SIM |url=https://www.vccircle.com/tatacommunications-to-take-full-control-of-oasis-smart-sim |work=[[VCCircle]] |date=July 11, 2023}}</ref> This was followed by the company's acquisition of The Switch Enterprises LLC in 2023, a United States-based live video production and transmission company, for approximately $58.8 million in an all-cash deal, to expand its media and entertainment services division.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Comm buys video co Switch for $59 mn |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/tata-comm-buys-video-co-switch-for-59-mn-11683143165091.html |work=[[Mint (newspaper)|Mint]] |date=May 4, 2023}}</ref>

In 2023, Tata Communications completed its acquisition of Kaleyra in a deal valued at approximately US$100 million. The acquisition combined the two companies' customer bases and enterprise communications businesses.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-10-08 |title=Tata Communications completes acquisition of US-based company Kaleyra |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/gadgets-news/tata-communications-completes-acquisition-of-us-based-company-kaleyra/articleshow/104247131.cms |access-date=2024-03-05 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

In 2025, the company acquired a 51% stake in Commotion Inc., an AI-native SaaS platform operating in the United States and India, for approximately ₹227 crore.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ksheerasagar |first=A |title=Tata Communications acquires 51% stake in US-based AI platform Commotion Inc. in ₹227 crore deal |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/tata-communications-acquires-51-stake-in-us-based-ai-platform-commotion-inc-in-rs-227-crore-deal-11764668812192.html |work=[[Mint (newspaper)|Mint]] |date=2 December 2025}}</ref>

=== Sports partnerships ===
In 2012, Tata Communications entered into a multi-year agreement with [[Formula One Management]] as the sport's official connectivity provider.<ref>{{cite news |last=Savage |first=Noor |title=Formula One's Telecom Partner |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/05/25/sports/autoracing/formula-ones-telecom-partner.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=24 May 2013}}</ref><ref name="fortune">{{cite news |title=The importance of being global |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/enterprise/the-importance-of-being-global/100249 |work=[[Fortune India]] |date=21 December 2016}}</ref> The company provided network connectivity and data services for [[Formula One]]'s global operations, including its official website.<ref name="fortune"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications leverages F1 partnership to innovate |url=https://www.autocarpro.in/feature/tata-communications-leverages-f1-partnership-innovate-22074 |work=Autocar Professional |date=7 October 2016}}</ref>

The agreement ended after the 2019 season. In 2022, the partnership was renewed, with Tata Communications becoming Formula One's official broadcast connectivity provider. The company transmitted video and audio feeds from race venues to the sport's media hub in the [[United Kingdom]].<ref>{{cite news |title=F1, Tata Communications announce multi-year strategic collaboration |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/f1-tata-communications-announce-multi-year-strategic-collaboration-326206-2022-03-16 |work=[[Business Today (India)|Business Today]] |date=16 March 2022}}</ref>

== Operations ==
Tata Communications operates through Voice and Data segments, providing telecommunications and digital products to enterprise customers. The Voice segment covers international and national long-distance telephony, while the [[Data]] segment comprises connectivity and related products such as [[Ethernet]], software-defined wide area networking (SD-WAN), [[content delivery network]], cloud, security, media and [[Internet of Things]].<ref name="livemint">{{cite news |last1=Ksheerasagar |first1=A. |last2=Grover |first2=Jatin |title=Tata Communications Q3 Results: Net profit jumps 55% YoY to ₹364 crore, revenue rises 7% |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/tata-communications-q3-results-net-profit-jumps-55-yoy-to-rs-364-crore-revenue-rises-7-11768987125502.html |work=[[Livemint|Mint]] |date=21 January 2026}}</ref>

The company also provides [[computing infrastructure|cloud infrastructure]] and [[artificial intelligence]] offerings. It describes its Digital Fabric platform as an architecture integrating network, cloud, interaction and IoT capabilities through a common orchestration layer.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications to deploy 'digital fabric' technology at all JLR sites |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/tata-communications-to-deploy-digital-fabric-technology-at-all-jlr-sites-123121200485_1.html |work=[[Business Standard]] |author=BS Web Team |date=12 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath launches IBM's AI GovTech Center to transform governance |url=https://telecom.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/enterprise-services/uttar-pradesh-cm-yogi-adityanath-launches-ibms-ai-govtech-center-to-transform-governance/128696681 |work=ET Telecom |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=23 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications launches AI-ready suite for enterprises |url=https://www.crnasia.com/news/2026/artificial-intelligence/tata-communications-launches-ai-ready-suite-for-enterprises |work=[[CRN (magazine)|CRN Asia]] |date=3 February 2026}}</ref>

== Financials ==
Tata Communications reported consolidated revenue of ₹23,109 crore for the financial year ending March 2025, compared to ₹20,969 crore in FY2024.<ref>{{cite news |title=Digital Fabric Boosts FY25 Revenue, PAT Up 44.7% |url=https://www.tatacommunications.com/press-release/q4-fy2025-financial-results |publisher=Tata Communications Investor Relations |date=22 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Comm records multi-fold jump in Q4 PAT; recommends final dividend of Rs 25/sh |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/tata-comm-records-multi-fold-jump-in-q4-pat-recommends-final-dividend-of-rs-25-sh-125042200981_1.html |work=[[Business Standard]] |date=22 April 2025}}</ref> Consolidated net profit (profit after tax) increased to ₹1,836 crore in FY2025, from ₹969 crore in FY2024.<ref name="FY25"/>

== Global network ==
In 2012, the company completed its network across [[Egypt]] linking [[Europe]] to [[India]], and created a subsea fibre network that circumnavigates the world. The {{convert|9,280|km|adj=on}} [[Eurasia]]n section of the Tata Global Network runs across the [[Mediterranean Sea]] and the [[Middle East]], connecting [[Mumbai]] with [[Marseille]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Tata Fiber Goes Around the World |url=https://www.lightreading.com/optical-networking/tata-fiber-goes-around-the-world |website=[[Light Reading]] |date=22 March 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications completes cable network ring around the world |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/tata-communications-completes-cable-network-ring-around-the-world/articleshow/12369028.cms |work=[[The Economic Times]]|date=22 March 2012}}</ref>

In January 2016, [[Windstream Holdings|Windstream Communications]] announced it was extending its [[100 Gigabit Ethernet]] (100G) network from [[New Jersey]] data center operator [[NJFX]]'s presence at Tata's Cable Landing Station (CLS) in [[Wall Township, New Jersey]], to [[Ashburn, Virginia]]'s internet hub.<ref>{{cite web |date=2016-01-19 |title=Windstream establishes 100G express route in red-hot Ashburn, Va. market via NJFX |url=http://www.fiercetelecom.com/story/windstream-establishes-100g-express-route-red-hot-ashburn-va-market-njfx/2016-01-19 |access-date=2016-01-30 |publisher=[[fiercetelecom.com]]}}</ref> As of 2016, Tata Communications had a [[Data center|data centre]] network located in 44 locations worldwide.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Balakrishnan |first=Reghu |date=2016-02-11 |title=ST Telemedia set to buy Tata Communications Data Centre |url=http://www.livemint.com/Companies/duDA19qCScOeLImvczvJ8H/ST-Telemedia-set-to-buy-Tata-Communications-Data-Centre.html |access-date=2017-05-10 |website=[[livemint.com]]}}</ref>

== Sustainability ==
It has set a target of achieving net-zero [[carbon emissions]] across its global operations by 2035.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications commits to net zero emissions by 2035 |url=https://telecom.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/enterprise-services/tata-communications-commits-to-net-zero-emissions-by-2035/99666742 |work=[[The Economic Times]] Telecom |date=21 April 2023}}</ref> Its greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets have been validated by the [[Science Based Targets initiative]], and the company has received an "A-" rating from the [[Carbon Disclosure Project]] for its climate disclosures.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tata Communications recognised with 'A-' score for leadership in sustainability by CDP |url=https://www.tataworld.com/news/openinside/tata-communications-recognised-by-cdp |publisher=Tata World |date=22 December 2020}}</ref>

The company has also adopted a sustainability-linked financing framework under which borrowing terms are tied to environmental performance targets.<ref name="business-standard">{{cite news |title=Tata Communications raises $250 million sustainability-linked loans |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/tata-communications-raises-250-million-sustainability-linked-loans-124062000927_1.html |work=[[Business Standard]] |date=20 June 2024}}</ref> In 2024, it raised a US$250 million sustainability-linked loan facility from [[ANZ (bank)|ANZ]], [[DBS Bank]], and [[Export Development Canada]], with interest rates linked to emissions reduction targets.<ref name="business-standard"/>

== Awards and recognition ==
In March 2026, [[Gartner]] positioned the company as a 'Leader' in its Magic Quadrant for Global WAN Services for the 13th consecutive year, citing its completeness of vision and ability to execute in the wide area network market.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications named Gartner WAN Leader for 13th consecutive year |url=https://indiantelevision.com/mam/tata-communications-named-gartner-wan-leader-for-13th-consecutive-year/ |work=Indian Television |date=31 March 2026}}</ref> 

In 2024 and 2025, Tata Communications received four ''Indian Service Provider Company of the Year'' awards from [[Frost & Sullivan]] in the SD-WAN, Unified Communications, Multi-Cloud Connect and next-generation connectivity categories<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Communications receives Frost & Sullivan’s 2025 Global Company of the Year Recognition for Leadership in Video Managed Services |url=https://www.frost.com/news/press-releases/tata-communications-receives-frost-sullivans-2025-global-company-of-the-year-recognition-for-leadership-in-video-managed-services/ |work=Frost & Sullivan |date=March 2025}}</ref>, and the ''Global Company of the Year Award'' in the Video Managed Services category.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tata Communications Recognized by Frost & Sullivan for Excellence in Next-gen Connectivity and Unified Communications |url=https://www.frost.com/news/press-releases/tata-communications-recognized-by-frost-sullivan-for-excellence-in-next-gen-connectivity-and-unified-communications/ |publisher=[[Frost & Sullivan]] |date=18 March 2024}}</ref>

The company has been included in the [[Fortune India 500]] ranking of India's largest companies by revenue since 2010, ranking 58th in 2010, 68th in 2015 and 2016, and 115th in 2025.<ref name="fortuneindia">{{cite web |title=Tata Communications Ltd Company Profile & Rankings |url=https://fortuneindia.com |work=[[Fortune India]]}}</ref>

Tata Communications Limited (formerly known as Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited) is an Indian telecommunications company, headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra. It was a government-owned telecommunications service provider before being sold to the Tata Group in 2002 under the Third Vajpayee ministry government.
The company provides network, cloud, cybersecurity, media, Internet of Things (IoT), collaboration and digital infrastructure services to enterprises and service providers worldwide. It is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India.
Tata Communications operates a Tier-1 IP network and a wholly owned subsea fibre-optic cable system spanning over 500,000 kilometres (310,000 miles). It provides services to enterprises across more than 190 countries and territories.
